    13  /-!
    14  # Monoid algebras
    15  
    16  When the domain of a `Finsupp` has a multiplicative or additive structure, we can define
    17  a convolution product. To mathematicians this structure is known as the "monoid algebra",
    18  i.e. the finite formal linear combinations over a given semiring of elements of a monoid `M`.
    19  The "group ring" `ℤ[G]` or the "group algebra" `k[G]` are typical uses.
    20  
    21  In fact the construction of the "monoid algebra" makes sense when `M` is not even a monoid, but
    22  merely a magma, i.e., when `M` carries a multiplication which is not required to satisfy any
    23  conditions at all. In this case the construction yields a not-necessarily-unital,
    24  not-necessarily-associative algebra but it is still adjoint to the forgetful functor from such
    25  algebras to magmas, and we prove this as `MonoidAlgebra.liftMagma`.
    26  
    27  In this file we define `MonoidAlgebra R M` and `AddMonoidAlgebra R M` as one-field structures around
    28  `M →₀ R`, and then define the convolution product on these.
    29  
    30  When the domain is additive, this is used to define polynomials:
    31  ```
    32  Polynomial R := AddMonoidAlgebra R ℕ
    33  MvPolynomial σ α := AddMonoidAlgebra R (σ →₀ ℕ)
    34  ```
    35  
    36  When the domain is multiplicative, e.g. a group, this will be used to define the group ring.
    37  
    38  ## Notation
    39  
    40  We introduce the notation `R[M]` for both `MonoidAlgebra R M` and `AddMonoidAlgebra R M`.
    41  The notations are scoped to their respective namespaces, and which one `R[M]` resolves to therefore
    42  depends on which of the two namespaces is open.
    43

    47  https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/36746
    48  https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/25273
    49  -/
